items.question: Suppose Voss-Lindqvist had paid Harrowgate USD 300,000 in fees in the year before the event giving rise to a claim. Would each party's liability under the signed MSA still be capped at USD 250,000?
items.answer:
The Harrowgate MSA's limitation of liability clause, Clause 8.1, states that each party's total aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of USD 250,000 or the Fees paid by the Client in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim [3].

Clause 4.1 of the Harrowgate MSA specifies that the Client shall pay a platform subscription fee of USD 18,500 per month for the Harrowgate platform [1].

If Voss-Lindqvist had paid Harrowgate USD 300,000 in fees in the year before the event giving rise to a claim, the liability cap would be the greater of USD 250,000 or the Fees paid, which in this case would be USD 300,000. Therefore, the liability would not be capped at USD 250,000 but would instead be capped at USD 300,000.

evidence.quote: Each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of USD 250,000 or the Fees paid by Client in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim
Client shall pay a platform subscription fee of USD 18,500 per month for the Harrowgate platform

items.question: Northbridge walks Voss-Lindqvist through its methodology on a video call and hands over nothing in writing. Can what was said still be Confidential Information under the NDA?
items.answer:
The Northbridge NDA defines "Confidential Information" in Clause 2.2. It states that Confidential Information includes all information disclosed by a Party (the "Discloser") to the other (the "Recipient") in connection with the Purpose, in any form, that is marked confidential or would reasonably be understood to be confidential [7].

The NDA also specifies that Confidential Information does not include information that the Recipient can show (a) is or becomes public other than through a breach of the Agreement; (b) was lawfully known to it before disclosure; (c) is independently developed without use of the Discloser's information; or (d) is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence [7].

The documents do not specify whether information disclosed in a video call without written documentation can still be considered Confidential Information. The NDA does not explicitly address whether verbal disclosures are included in the definition of Confidential Information. However, the definition includes "all information disclosed... in any form," which could be interpreted to include verbal disclosures. The NDA does not clarify whether verbal disclosures are included in the definition of Confidential Information.
